meta.note: Derived from article-cards-models.json. Mirrors reviews-expressions.json (moves > function > sub-function) so the sample reader needs no genre-specific code, with two additions. 'frame' is the teachable lead-in — the segment BEFORE the first gap, which is the part a learner reuses; taking the longest segment instead lands on the tail and teaches nothing. 'match' is a ladder of literals, longest first: the full frame with slash alternatives expanded, then every prefix down to three words that actually occurs in the samples. The reader marks the first that hits and stops, so a phrase is never marked twice, but a sample that paraphrases the tail — 'For me personally, the most significant change' against a pool that says 'the best thing about' — still gets its opening frame marked. Two guards keep the ladder honest: a prefix that would also open a different entry's frame is rejected, so no phrase is labelled as the wrong move; and a prefix ending on a function word is rejected, so nothing is marked mid-clause. Regenerate this file whenever the pools or the samples change.
